Customer/Renter Survey Questionnaire
The adopted Customer/Renter Survey Questionnaire contains 38 statements
across nine sections: Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Compatibility,
Interaction Capability, Reliability, Security, Maintainability, Flexibility, and Safety.
Customer/Renter item A4 will use the documented wording adaptation matching the
Finder’s implemented criteria. The remaining 37 customer statements and the
four-point scale will be retained. Customer responses will reflect experience with the
booking and vehicle-selection workflow. Ratings of maintainability and security will be
interpreted as customer perceptions and supported separately by technical evidence;
they will not establish source-code modifiability or security effectiveness.
A. Functional Suitability
In the ISO/IEC 25010 definition, functional suitability refers to how well a
product or system provides the right functions to meet user needs under specified
conditions, ensuring that all required functions are present, work correctly, and
effectively support users in achieving their intended tasks and objectives.
The following statements are retained in the adopted survey instrument:
● The system provides the necessary features for submitting a car rental booking
request.
● The vehicle catalog allows customers to view available vehicles clearly.
● The customer-side vehicle recommendation feature allows customers to input
travel requirements before booking.
● The vehicle recommendation feature suggests available vehicles for the
selected rental dates that meet passenger and luggage requirements and the
estimated base-rental budget, and prioritizes the preferred vehicle category.
● The system allows customers to upload rental requirements and proof of
payment properly.
● The system allows customers to track their booking status.
These questions specifically address whether the system offers complete and
appropriate customer-side features, covers essential booking functions, and supports
vehicle selection before booking. By directly targeting these functional areas, the
questions together measure the system’s functional suitability from the customer
perspective.
B. Performance Efficiency
In the ISO/IEC 25010 definition, performance efficiency refers to the degree to
which a product or system performs its functions within specified time and throughput
parameters while efficiently utilizing resources under specified conditions.
The following statements are retained in the adopted survey instrument:
● The system loads pages and forms within an acceptable time.
● The customer-side vehicle recommendation feature processes customer inputs
without unnecessary delay.
● The system allows customers to submit booking requests efficiently.
● The system allows customers to upload requirements and proof of payment
without noticeable delay.
These questions include response time, processing speed, booking submission,
and file upload performance. These elements help assess the efficiency of the
customer-side system from the perspective of the renter.
C. Compatibility
In the ISO/IEC 25010 definition, compatibility refers to the degree to which a
product, system, or component can perform its required functions while sharing a
common environment and resources.
The following statements are retained in the adopted survey instrument:
● The system works properly on the device being used.
● The system can be accessed through common web browsers.
● The system interface remains usable on desktop and mobile browsers.
● The customer-side features work properly across supported devices.
These questions check whether the system works correctly across different
user devices and common browsers. They help measure how compatible the system is
for customers who may use laptops, tablets, or mobile phones.
D. Interaction Capability
In the ISO/IEC 25010 definition, interaction capability refers to the degree to
which a product or system can be effectively interacted with by specified users through
its user interface to exchange information and complete tasks in various contexts of
use.
The following statements are retained in the adopted survey instrument:
● The system is easy to understand and operate.
● The labels, buttons, and forms are clear.
● The customer-side vehicle recommendation feature is easy to use when
selecting a suitable vehicle.
● Booking-related tasks can be completed without confusion.
● The system provides clear messages, prompts, and notifications.
These questions assess ease of use, independent task completion, clarity of
design, and the ability of customers to complete system tasks without confusion.
E. Reliability
According to ISO/IEC 25010, reliability refers to the degree to which a system
performs specified functions consistently and accurately under stated conditions for a
specified period of time.
The following statements are retained in the adopted survey instrument:
● The system performs its customer-side functions consistently.
● The system accurately records booking requests.
● The system properly handles incomplete or incorrect customer inputs.
● The system provides accurate booking status updates.
These questions assess whether the system can consistently support customer
transactions and provide correct outputs during customer use.
F. Security
According to ISO/IEC 25010, security is the degree to which a system protects
information and data so that unauthorized persons or systems cannot access, modify,
or misuse them.
The following statements are retained in the adopted survey instrument:
● The system requires customers to log in before accessing their booking
records.

Validity and Reliability of the Instrument
The original adopted instrument, its cited sources, and the revised adopted
version will be retained for traceability. The revision record will identify the wording
adaptation to Customer/Renter A4, restoration of missing response checkboxes in
business-user F5 and G4, and the clarified role-specific and unscored-response
instructions. Before administration, qualified reviewers will assess the revised
instrument’s suitability for the car-rental setting, clarity, role applicability, and
correspondence between its quality sections and available evidence. Adoption and
revision do not establish that content validation or reliability testing has already been
completed. Any further approved change to an item or response scale will be
documented and the administered version identified.
Review will cover software or IT evaluation, research methods or statistics, and
language clarity. Reviewer qualifications, comments, and decisions will be
documented. Reviewers will assess the Customer/Renter A4 adaptation and the
clarified administration instructions, including items respondents cannot judge and
statements concerning future capabilities. The revised adopted version will be
submitted for review before administration; approval and completed validation will be
reported only when supporting records exist.
The adopted questionnaires will be pilot-tested before final administration with
eligible participants excluded from the final evaluation sample. The pilot will check
instructions, task exposure, item interpretation, completion burden, and response
variation. Pilot recruitment and the adequacy of responses will be agreed with the
research/statistics reviewer in relation to the items and respondent groups. Cronbach’s
alpha will be considered separately for coherent multi-item characteristics when
sufficient complete responses are available; different roles and different characteristics
will not be pooled merely to obtain a coefficient. The small business-user and expert
groups will not support strong reliability claims. Pilot counts, administration issues, any
computable coefficients, and limitations will be reported. No reliability result is claimed
before these data are collected.
Ethical Considerations
Ethical considerations will be observed throughout the conduct of the study to
ensure responsible, respectful, and lawful handling of data during requirements
gathering, system development, testing, and evaluation. Since the proposed system
will involve customer information, booking records, uploaded requirements, proof of
payment, vehicle records, rental transactions, maintenance records, and operational
reports, the proponents will ensure that data privacy and confidentiality are maintained.
Before conducting interviews, surveys, testing, or evaluation, the participants
will be informed about the purpose of the study and their role in the research.
Participation will be voluntary, and respondents will have the right to refuse or withdraw
from the activity without any penalty. The information gathered from respondents will be
used only for academic and system development purposes.
The study will also observe the principles of the Data Privacy Act of 2012, or
Republic Act No. 10173. No real client booking or rental records are used in the current
development and evaluation dataset. The synthetic records will not contain real
customer identities, contact information, identification documents, proof of payment, or
other personal client data. If verified client records are obtained for a later authorized
evaluation, the proponents will minimize, mask, or anonymize identifiable information
and analyze those records separately from the synthetic dataset. Current synthetic
results will remain clearly labeled and will not be presented as measured real-world
forecasting performance.
The proposed system will also be designed to protect data through secure
authentication, role-based access control, and restricted access to sensitive records.
Customers will only be allowed to access their own account, booking details, uploaded
requirements, and payment proof. Administrators will be allowed to manage operational
records based on their assigned responsibilities. Owners will have access to financial,
reporting, and decision-support functions.
The study will not include unauthorized tracking of vehicles or individuals.
Although the client uses existing tools such as AKSH GPS, Apple Find My, and
AirTags, the proposed system will not directly integrate live GPS tracking. The system
will only record vehicle status, monitoring notes, rental status, condition records, and
maintenance-related updates entered by authorized users. This ensures that the
system remains aligned with its declared scope and avoids privacy concerns related to
live location monitoring.
The proponents will also maintain academic integrity by properly citing all
related literature, studies, systems, frameworks, and standards used in the manuscript.
The proponents will not fabricate data, manipulate evaluation results, or claim features
that are not included in the developed system.
Data Analysis (Procedure and Treatment)
After the system evaluation, the collected questionnaire responses will be
checked, tabulated, and analyzed according to respondent group and ISO/IEC 25010
quality characteristics. The responses of customer or renter respondents will be used
to evaluate customer-side features such as account registration, Customer-Side
Vehicle Recommendation, vehicle browsing, booking request submission, requirement
upload, proof-of-payment submission, booking status tracking, notifications, rental
policy viewing, and ease of use.
Owner/Admin responses will describe administrative functions and
decision-support review, while Operations Staff responses will describe only their
permitted operational functions. IT expert responses will be accompanied by technical
and functional test evidence, including source/database inspection where relevant.
Results will remain separate by role so that staff are not represented as having
evaluated restricted forecasting, allocation, payment-review, or
maintenance-management functions.
Questionnaire responses will be summarized using frequency counts,
percentages, item-level weighted means, and descriptive interpretations. Each item’s
denominator will include only valid scored responses from the eligible respondent
group. Restricted, unobserved, and missing responses will be excluded and their
counts reported. Characteristic summaries will include only applicable items and will
remain separate by role. Ratings indicate participant assessments under the tested
conditions; technical correctness, security, and reliability claims will also require the
corresponding test evidence.
Because no real historical client records are currently available, Mean Absolute
Percentage Error will be used only to verify forecast-error computation within the
labeled synthetic time series. The calculation will match original Week +1 forecasts with
the realized synthetic qualifying-demand values for the same branch, vehicle category,
and target week and will report the synthetic coverage period, valid observation count,
and excluded zero-demand periods. The resulting MAPE will be described as a
functional-test result, not as evidence of empirical predictive accuracy, seasonal
performance, or long-term operational effectiveness. A separate real-world accuracy
evaluation may only be conducted if sufficient verified client or post-implementation
observations later become available.

Ranking
Ranking will describe higher- and lower-rated applicable characteristics within
the same respondent group. Tied means will receive tied ranks. Rankings will not be
used to compare groups that rated different items or to imply statistically significant
differences.
Mean Absolute Percentage Error
Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) will be used to verify the observed
error calculation of the Weighted Moving Average forecasts within the labeled synthetic
test dataset. In this evaluation, actual demand means the realized qualifying booking
count for a completed week in the synthetic time series and does not represent
empirical client demand. Forecast and realized values shall refer to the same branch,
vehicle category, and weekly period, and the forecast used shall be the value originally
generated when the target period was one week ahead. The evaluation shall follow the
snapshot and timing rules in the forecasting methodology and report the evaluated
branch-category series, synthetic coverage period, number of valid observations, and
excluded zero-demand weeks. MAPE shall include only observations where the
realized synthetic demand is greater than zero because percentage error is undefined
when the denominator is zero. Zero-demand periods shall be reported separately and
excluded from the MAPE divisor. Lower MAPE values indicate smaller errors within the
synthetic test series, but the result shall be reported only as evidence of computational
behavior and rule conformance. It shall not be interpreted as real-world predictive
accuracy, seasonal validity, or long-term operational effectiveness, and no qualitative
accuracy classification shall be assigned.
Formula:
MAPE = (1/n) Σ |(Actual Value - Forecasted Value) / Actual Value| × 100
Where:
n = number of observations
Actual Value = actual demand value
Forecasted Value = demand value estimated by the system
